en: Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with wet floors, preventing you from slipping and falling.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause a dangerous shock.
Always use a dry cloth pot holder when holding a hot pan because cloth is a thermal insulator that prevents burns.
Wearing earplugs at loud concerts reduces sound wave intensity to protect your delicate eardrums from permanent hearing damage.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light rays that can permanently damage your eyes' retinas.
Store heavy books on the bottom shelf so gravity does not pull them down onto your head or feet.
Never swallow small magnetic toys because they can attract each other inside your intestines and cause severe tissue damage.
Using a wheelbarrow combines a lever and a wheel-and-axle to help you move heavy garden soil with less effort.
Eating rice gives your body chemical energy, which your muscles convert into mechanical energy to ride a bicycle.
Metal pots have plastic handles because plastic is a poor conductor of heat that protects your hands from burning.
A ramp is an inclined plane that lets you push a heavy wheelchair up safely instead of lifting it.
Touch a metal doorknob after walking on a carpet to safely discharge static electricity and avoid a painful shock.
